differences.what: massing: the draft's flat-roofed generic block is now the engraving's Italianate house, two storeys over a raised basement under a low hipped roof, the cornice's bed near 11.5 m; front on the right, shaded south flank receding left, as the engraving draws them
the deep cornice on paired scrolled brackets over a panelled frieze, carried along the front and the south flank
the porch on columns at the stoop's head, its flat top a balcony with a stone balustrade before the arched window over the door
the high stoop onto a terrace across the front, its cheeks scrolled at their foot, and the front's round-headed windows under hoods with keystones in both storeys
the low stone wall along the walk, with the stoop's opening

the porch: the engraving draws its balcony about twice as wide as the window spacing beside it allows (x 740-867 px) and the window over the door at the balcony's north end. T-3239 widens the porch from 4.0 to 5.0 m (v 6.7-11.7), the 1898 vignette's portico (about 4.7 m against the door-to-window spacing, its camera tribune_1898_front); the vignette draws the window over the door on the door's axis, as built, so where it stands is a gap the two pictures disagree about

the left of the picture: the engraving's large block at the south flank's front, with its own bracketed cornice, a columned porch under a balustraded balcony and round-headed windows, and the terrace's balustrade running before it (x 100-430 px); the render has the sheet's brick range along the flank instead. Neither the vignette nor the c. 1914 elevation drawing sees the flank, so nothing confirms or sizes it, and K01 stands a porch and balcony only at the entrance (k07 door hood) or as a terrace loggia at the stoop: a side porch on a flank pavilion is more than this sign-off's run, so it stays open here under AGENTS.md rule 11

the tower: the render's south bay rose a full 3.4 m stage over the cornice, narrow (a 2.0 m ring); the engraving's is lower and broader, and the vignette and the c. 1914 elevation drawing both stop it at about the main cornice. T-3239 broadens the ring to 2.6 m (v 0.4-5.6, the vignette's tower about 5.5 m across) and lowers it to four stages of 2.34, 4.4, 3.5 and 3.0 m, its wall head 13.24 m, 1.1 m over the main wall's 12.14 m (the least K01 lets a tower clear its host's eave by is 1.0 m) under its hipped cap with cresting

the roof's balustraded deck and its tall stack over the south flank, which the render does not have; the c. 1914 elevation drawing agrees, drawing the hip flat-topped with a tall stack at the south end. K01's hip roof takes no railed deck (only a flat roof is a deck, behind parapets), so it stays open here

the curved flights of the stoop's foot: the engraving splays them out to the walk; the 1898 vignette draws the flight straight between its cheeks, ending at block newels, as built (scrolled cheek ends rather than newels): a gap the two pictures disagree about

the terrace's balustrade: T-3239 sets the turned stone balustrade (1620's, K07) on both terraces and down the stoop's cheeks, as the engraving and the vignette both draw it, from the south tower to the stoop and from the stoop to the stone front's north end; its run before the flank's block is that block's (open above)
colour: the engraving is monochrome; the brownstone front and the brick flanks are the census ruling's and the rules'
the north flank, the rear wing and the rear, which the engraving does not see

_how: verdict is unreviewed | differs | matches, set by whoever compared the side-by-side with the picture; each difference is {what, status: open | fixed | not shown | within tolerance | owner ruling} — open only if a street visitor would notice it (over about 1 ft, missing, mis-shaped, miscounted, wrong material or colour), else within tolerance (T-3153); owner ruling where the owner asked the build to depart from the picture (T-3236).
